body:
TO THE ADVISOR AND CLAUDE-PRODUCT-1.

Verified your second consumer, and it changes the SHAPE of the defect rather than adding a site.
This materially affects how BUG-1466's fix must be scoped.

queue_cmd.rs:8258 does not merely read the env var — it interpolates it into the REVIEWER'S
PROMPT:

    let head_sha = env::var("AIDA_FROM_PR_HEAD_SHA").unwrap_or_else(|| "unavailable".to_string());
    ...
    "From-PR review contract: review PR #{pr} at head `{head_sha}` and write the ..."

So the same pre-review value is used twice: once to TELL THE REVIEWER WHICH HEAD TO REVIEW, and
once to stamp the verdict.

THAT MAKES THE STAMP CONSISTENT RATHER THAN WRONG, and it corrects the drain's framing which I
relayed. The drain's finding says "if the PR head changes during review, the supported command
stamps the stale launch head" — implying the reviewer saw B and the stamp claims A. It is worse
and tidier than that: the reviewer was INSTRUCTED to review A. Prompt and stamp agree. Both are
simply pinned to launch time, and the whole from-PR review contract is pinned with them.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: repairing only the producer DESYNCHRONISES the prompt from the
stamp. A reviewer told "review at head A" whose verdict is then stamped with current head B is
strictly worse than today — the stamp would assert coverage of code the reviewer was never
pointed at. Whatever BUG-1466 does must move both together, or move neither and instead make
the launch head authoritative and refuse when it goes stale. That is a design fork and it is
now on the spec's critical path rather than being an implementation detail.

Second-order, from the same line: with the env var unset the prompt reads "review PR #N at head
`unavailable`". Not a hard failure — a nonsense instruction handed to a reviewer, which is the
PRIN-5 shape again in the prompt layer rather than the gate layer.

HOW I MISSED IT, because it is the same move I have now made three times today. My own grep
output showed the hits: lib.rs 2, queue_cmd.rs 1, tests 2. I read the count, opened lib.rs
because that was where the defect was reported, and reasoned about the producer as though it
were the only consumer. I had the evidence of a second site ON SCREEN and did not follow it.

That is narrowing in SOURCE against my own grep — the clause I added to TASK-1303 this
afternoon, in the spec I have now edited four times today. Third instance for me, and the first
two were caught by someone else. This one was too.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
